artists.biography: Gravediggaz is an American hip hop group from New York City, well known for its dark sense of humor and abrasive, menacing soundscapes. The group was formed in 1994 and was effectively a supergroup, bringing together Prince Paul (The Undertaker), Frukwan (The Gatekeeper), Too Poetic (The Grym Reaper) and RZA (The Rzarector). Its inception was largely due to the efforts of Prince Paul. The group is widely credited as being one of the most influential and pioneering groups in the small hip-hop subgenre of horrorcore.

perplexity.description:
6 Feet Deep, released on August 9, 1994, is the debut album by Gravediggaz, a supergroup credited with pioneering the horrorcore subgenre of hip hop. The album features dark, eerie production primarily overseen by Prince Paul, blending spooky, death-themed lyrics with a mix of grim storytelling and dark humor. This conceptual approach set it apart from mainstream hip hop of the time, with tracks like "Diary of a Madman" and "Nowhere to Run, Nowhere to Hide" showcasing the group's unique style and RZA's distinctive production influence.

As Gravediggaz's first major release, 6 Feet Deep holds a significant place in their discography as a groundbreaking project that introduced horrorcore to a wider audience. Although it did not achieve major commercial success upon release, the album received favorable reviews and has since developed a cult following for its innovative fusion of horror themes and hip hop. The album was released by Gee Street Records (not HHC Records) and is sometimes known by its alternate title Niggamortis outside the United States.

Critically, the album was praised for its originality and production quality, with Prince Paul’s conceptual vision and RZA’s contributions standing out. Despite modest sales, 6 Feet Deep is regarded as an influential work that helped shape a niche within hip hop, blending macabre storytelling with complex beats and lyrical skill.
